questions.questionText: Which statement about factors of production is correct?

options.text: Capital is the money people keep in the bank.
Enterprise is found more in service industries than in manufacturing industries.
Labour includes only those who work using their hands.
Land includes resources found in or under the sea.

questions.questionText:
China earns enough income to purchase large quantities of natural resources from developing
countries.
Which statement explains this situation?

options.text: China does not experience the economic problem of scarcity.
Supplies of natural resources in China are limited relative to demand.
There are unlimited supplies of natural resources in developing countries.
There is an excess stock of land in China.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows the change in an economy’s production possibility curve from year 1 to
year 2.
goods
year 2
year 1
services
What might explain the change from year 1 to year 2?

options.text: Resources have moved from the production of services to the production of goods.
The number of workers unemployed in manufacturing has fallen.
The producers of services have introduced better technology.
The workers in the production of goods have become less efficient.

questions.questionText:
As incomes have risen in India, cinema attendance has increased.
How would this change be shown on a demand and supply diagram?
demand curve for supply curve of
cinema tickets cinema tickets

options.text: movement along shifts to the left
movement along shifts to the right
shifts to the left movement along
shifts to the right movement along

questions.questionText:
Although some economists believe that resources should be allocated through market forces,
markets often fail.
What might be an example of market failure?

options.text: access to subsidised health care
monopoly pricing of electricity supplies
prohibiting cigarette smoking in public places
regulation of interest rates charged by banks

questions.questionText:
A group of shops sells all its products at the same price of $1. It is still able to make a profit,
although in other shops the products are sold at a higher price.
Which statement about this group of shops must be correct?

options.text: Consumers recognise that the group’s products are better value.
Costs will be lower than in the other shops.
Revenue will be less than in the other shops.
The group does not advertise nor use any form of marketing.

questions.questionText:
In 2011, the Bank of England released into circulation a new design for the £50 note to replace
the old design £50 note.
What might have been the reason for issuing these notes?

options.text: to ease the use of the barter system
to enable a means of exchange
to lower the external value of the £ sterling
to reduce inflationary pressures in the economy

percentage of total population percentage of total population
in five-year age and sex groups in five-year age and sex groups
What can be concluded from these pyramids?

options.text: country X has the highest population
country X is more typical of a developed country
country Y has a higher birth rate
country Y has a lower dependency rate

questions.questionText:
A security company wishes to recruit an experienced person for a senior position to answer
customers’ emergency calls, some of which would be during the night. It is offering a good salary
and a small apartment next to the company premises.
Which person would be most likely to apply and be offered the position?

options.text: a confident person currently employed in installing security systems for the company
a person who has experience of answering customers’ queries in a travel company
a recently qualified engineering graduate in security systems
a reliable person who says that he needs to live with his young family of five children

questions.questionText: Why do female workers in many countries have a lower income than male workers?

options.text: Female workers are more experienced.
Female workers are more likely to be employed part-time.
Female workers are more likely to be in trade unions.
Female workers have more qualifications.

questions.questionText:
India is experiencing rapid growth in air travel. The number and size of airlines is increasing every
year.
Which effect arising from this growth is an external economy of scale?

options.text: Banks are more prepared to lend to large airlines rather than small airlines.
Colleges are established to train flight crew.
Fuel suppliers charge less to airlines that buy in bulk.
Larger airlines operate aircraft which can carry more passengers.

questions.questionText:
The financial director of a company adds up the cost for the firm of rent, insurance, new
machinery and the chief executive’s basic salary. The director then divides that total by the firm’s
output.
What has the director calculated?

options.text: average fixed cost
average revenue
average total cost
average variable cost

questions.questionText:
If a perfectly competitive market becomes a monopoly, what will be likely to increase and what
will be likely to decrease?
increase decrease

options.text: barriers to entry economies of scale
consumer choice prices
long-run profits competition
output market share

questions.questionText:
A government achieves a high rate of economic growth.
What may result from this that might cause a conflict with other government aims?

options.text: it may increase government income
it may increase incomes for the lower paid
it may increase the supply of exports
it may increase the volume of imports

questions.questionText: What type of tax is a tax of 10% on the price of petrol?

options.text: a direct tax
a progressive tax
an income tax
an indirect tax

questions.questionText: What could a government in a developed economy do to decrease demand?

options.text: create a budget deficit
increase government spending
increase taxes
reduce interest rates

questions.questionText:
A country closed its oil wells because it had used up most of its supplies of oil.
What type of unemployment would this cause?

options.text: cyclical
frictional
seasonal
structural

questions.questionText:
In a country, in one year, average transport prices rose by 15% and the price of electrical
products fell by 15%. The two products had equal weights in the retail price index.
If no other prices changed, what happened to the index?

options.text: It fell by less than 15%.
It fell by over 15%.
It remained unchanged.
It rose by less than 15%.

questions.questionText:
There is a decrease in a country’s birth rate.
What must occur at the same time to lead to an increase in the country’s population?

options.text: positive net migration and a fall in the death rate
positive net migration and a fall in the fertility rate
zero net migration and a fall in infant mortality
zero net migration and a fall in the fertility rate

questions.questionText:
In 2008, the Peruvian Government set itself the target of reducing the number of its people in
poverty to 30% of the population.
What change does not indicate that the Peruvian Government had made progress towards this
objective?

options.text: a rise in employment
a rise in infant mortality
a rise in life expectancy
a rise in the level of adult literacy

questions.questionText: Which would cause a favourable change in the Kenyan trade in services (invisible) account?

options.text: A Kenyan company wins a contract to transport exports from Uganda.
A Kenyan tea company increases its exports.
A Kenyan trade delegation visits India.
A Zambian company increases its exports to Kenya.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from an extension of specialisation in manufacturing?

options.text: for the consumer some prices will be reduced
for the country there will be less dependency on international trade
for the employee the work will become more varied
for the producer there will be less efficiency

questions.questionText: What would reduce the volume of international trade in the world economy?

options.text: a German bank making a loan to a Nigerian company
a Japanese car manufacturer establishing a factory in the Czech Republic
the Canadian Government introducing quotas on Malaysian electronics products
the Swedish Government granting aid to Somalia

questions.questionText:
The table shows the number of units of four currencies which exchanged for one US$ in 2003
and 2013.
In which country’s currency would imports have become cheaper?
country’s currency 2003 2013
